   119	/// The most hidden regions one layer may carry.
   120	///
   121	/// A SHADER BUDGET, exactly as [`crate::model::MAX_FILTERS`] is: the
   122	/// uniform block carries four regions and the fragment stage applies them
   123	/// in a fixed unrolled order, so a fifth has nowhere to go. `set_video`
   124	/// names the overflow rather than dropping it, and the reason is sharper
   125	/// here than it is for a filter — a region the user drew over a face and
   126	/// cannot see is not a control that does nothing, it is the face still on
   127	/// screen.
   128	pub const MAX_OBSCURE: usize = 4;
   129	
   130	/// One region of the picture hidden behind a blur or a pixelation (road map
   131	/// 2, phase 3c) — the spotlight's inverse. A face, a password field, a
   132	/// notification that slid in halfway through the take.
   133	///
   134	/// The geometry is [`Spotlight`]'s frame, and the paragraph above that type
   135	/// is its canonical statement: `x`/`y` are the region's CENTRE as an offset
   136	/// in SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect, `width`
   137	/// and `height` its size in the same pixels. So a region rides with its
   138	/// layer through scale, move and rotation, and stays on the face it was put
   139	/// on. Nothing here is in canvas pixels, and a nest's transform folds into
   140	/// the layer around it rather than into this box.
   141	///
   142	/// `shape` is [`SpotShape`] — the spotlight's own rect/ellipse, reused
   143	/// rather than copied. It is the same vocabulary naming the same distance
   144	/// field, and shared vocabulary has exactly one home (core/CLAUDE.md); if
   145	/// the two ever have to diverge, splitting an enum is a rename, while
   146	/// merging two is a schema migration.
   147	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   148	#[serde(default)]
   149	pub struct ObscureRegion {
   150	    pub shape: SpotShape,
   151	    pub x: f64,
   152	    pub y: f64,
   153	    pub width: f64,
   154	    pub height: f64,
   155	    /// Source pixels the effect is ramped in over; 0 is a hard edge.
   156	    pub feather: f64,
   157	    pub kind: ObscureKind,
   158	    /// 0 = the region is there but hides nothing, 1 = its full effect.
   159	    pub amount: f64,
   160	}
   161	
   162	impl Default for ObscureRegion {
   163	    /// A 480 × 270 window, centred — [`Spotlight`]'s own default box, so
   164	    /// the two region controls put the SAME rectangle on screen and a user
   165	    /// who has met one recognises the other — pixelated at full strength.
   166	    ///
   167	    /// The kind and the amount are the opposite of
   168	    /// [`crate::model::Filter`]'s half-strength blur, for the opposite
   169	    /// reason. A filter has to be visible without destroying the frame; a
   170	    /// region that only half hides has failed at the one job this feature
   171	    /// has, so its default is the setting that actually hides. Between the
   172	    /// two kinds that is `pixelate`: a blur at the shader's maximum radius
   173	    /// is a SOFT blur — a large password field can still be read through
   174	    /// it — while a pixelation at full strength destroys the detail
   175	    /// outright.
   176	    ///
   177	    /// `feather` is 20 rather than the spotlight's 40 because a region put
   178	    /// over a face is usually much smaller than a callout window, and a
   179	    /// 40-pixel ramp on a 200-pixel box is mostly ramp.
   180	    fn default() -> Self {
   181	        ObscureRegion {
   182	            shape: SpotShape::Rect,
   183	            x: 0.0,
   184	            y: 0.0,
   185	            width: 480.0,
   186	            height: 270.0,
   187	            feather: 20.0,
   188	            kind: ObscureKind::Pixelate,
   189	            amount: 1.0,
   190	        }
   191	    }
   192	}
   193	
   194	/// How a region hides what is under it.
   195	///
   196	/// Closed at two, and a type of its own rather than a
   197	/// [`crate::model::FilterKind`] restricted to two of its seven: a range
   198	/// check that had to say "kind must be blur or pixelate" would be a rule
   199	/// about a type enforced a long way from it, which is what `props_check.rs`
   200	/// argues against, and serde would take `"sepia"` out of a hand-written
   201	/// file into a field nothing downstream could repair — there is no neutral
   202	/// obscure kind to fall back to, the way a filter's `amount` can fall back
   203	/// to 0. A closed enum makes the illegal state unrepresentable and hands
   204	/// the shader a two-value discriminant.
   205	///
   206	/// Declaration order is that discriminant's order (`ProjectSnapshot.swift`
   207	/// derives `shaderCode` from the case index and `Compositor.metal` reads
   208	/// the number), so a kind may be added at the END but the two here must
   209	/// never be swapped.
   210	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   211	#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
   212	pub enum ObscureKind {
   213	    Blur,
   214	    /// The default, and [`ObscureRegion::default`] says why: it is the kind
   215	    /// that actually hides.
   216	    #[default]
   217	    Pixelate,
   218	}

1	---
     2	title: Obscure
     3	description: Hide a face, a password or a phone number behind pixelated or blurred regions that stay on the clip as it moves.
     4	---
     5	
     6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
     7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
     8	
     9	Obscure hides part of a clip's picture, such as a face, a password field or a phone number, behind a pixelated or blurred region. A clip can carry up to four regions.
    10	
    11	<AtAGlance
    12	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Obscure"
    13	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
    14	/>
    15	
    16	## Draw a region on the picture
    17	
    18	<Steps>
    19	
    20	1. Select the clip, and move the playhead to a frame that shows what you want to hide.
    21	
    22	2. In the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, open the **Obscure** section. It's shut until you open it.
    23	
    24	3. Choose **Place on Canvas**. The preview reads "Drag a rectangle to obscure · Esc to cancel".
    25	
    26	4. Drag a rectangle over what you want to hide.
    27	
    28	</Steps>
    29	
    30	The region lands pixelated at full strength, and it's one undo step, called Obscure Region. Its controls appear in the section as **Region 1**, **Region 2** and so on.
    31	
    32	A region lasts the whole clip and keeps its place on the clip's picture. It doesn't track anything that moves in the footage. To hide something for part of a clip, [split](/editing/splitting/) the clip first and put the region on the piece that needs it. To follow something across the shot, [animate the region](#animate-a-region).
    33	
    34	Place on Canvas draws one region and then ends. It needs exactly one selected clip, drawing at the playhead and not on a locked track, with fewer than four regions. Otherwise it beeps, and at four regions the button is greyed.
    35	
    36	While you're drawing:
    37	
    38	- You can start the drag outside the picture, which is the way to catch the edge of the frame.
    39	- A drag under 6 canvas pixels wide or tall counts as a miss. It beeps and you can draw again.
    40	- <kbd>Esc</kbd> or a second press of **Place on Canvas** stops without adding anything. After a click in the inspector, <kbd>Esc</kbd> no longer reaches the preview, so use the button.
    41	- Changing the selection, or moving the playhead off the clip, also stops it.
    42	
    43	Only one mode that waits for a click or drag on the preview can be on at a time: Place on Canvas, [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/), [Chroma Key's Pick from Canvas](/effects/chroma-key/) and the [qualifier's Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/). Turning one on ends the other.
    44	
    45	## Add a region without drawing
    46	
    47	**Add Region** puts a 480 × 270 region at the centre of the clip, as one undo step called Add Region. It's a **Rectangle**, set to **Pixelate** at 100 % **Amount** with 20 px **Feather**. A region you draw takes the same settings, apart from its position and size.
    48	
    49	The button is greyed at four regions, and the note beside it reads "4 at most". With no regions, the section reads "No obscured regions."
    50	
    51	## Choose Pixelate or Blur
    52	
    53	The pop-up in each **Region** row sets how the region hides what's under it.
    54	
    55	| Kind | What it does | At 100 % Amount |
    56	| --- | --- | --- |
    57	| **Pixelate** | Replaces the picture with coarse blocks, destroying the detail. This is the default. | Blocks 64 of the clip's own pixels across |
    58	| **Blur** | Softens the picture. | A blur reaching 24 of the clip's own pixels |
    59	
    60	:::caution
    61	Blur at its strongest is still a soft blur, and large text can be read through it. Use **Pixelate** for anything that must not be read.
    62	:::
    63	
    64	Both are measured in the clip's own pixels, so they grow and shrink with the clip. On a 4K recording, the same blocks cover half the width of the picture they would on a 1080p one. Check that what you've hidden stays hidden at the size you'll export.
    65	
    66	## The region controls
    67	
    68	Each region has its own group of rows.
    69	
    70	| Control | What it does | Default | Range | Quick picks |
    71	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    72	| **Region 1** pop-up | The kind, [Pixelate or Blur](#choose-pixelate-or-blur). | Pixelate | | |
    73	| **Shape** | The outline of the region. | Rectangle | Rectangle, Ellipse | |
    74	| **Amount** | How strongly it hides. At 0 % the region is there and hides nothing. | 100 % | 0 to 100 % | 0, 25, 50, 75, 100 |
    75	| **Feather** | How wide the ramp is over the region's edge. At 0 the edge is hard. | 20 px | 0 to 200 px | 0, 10, 20, 40, 80 |
    76	| **Center** | Where the region's centre sits, as x and y from the centre of the clip's picture, with y counting down. | 0, 0 | −20,000 to 20,000 px | |
    77	| **Size** | The region's width and height. | 480 × 270 | 1 to 20,000 px | Width 120, 240, 480, 960. Height 68, 135, 270, 540 |
    78	
    79	**Center** and **Size** are in the clip's own pixels, not the canvas's, so 480 × 270 covers less of a 4K recording than of a 1080p one. A region can sit partly or wholly off the clip.
    80	
    81	**Feather** straddles the outline, half inside and half outside. At 20 px the effect is at full strength only from 10 px inside the outline, so leave a margin around anything that must stay hidden.
    82	
    83	## Move and resize a region on the canvas
    84	
    85	Select one clip and its regions draw on the preview as dashed outlines, each with a cross at its centre and eight handles.
    86	
    87	| To | Do this |
    88	| --- | --- |
    89	| Move a region | Drag its centre cross. |
    90	| Resize a region | Drag one of its handles. The far edge stays where it is. |
    91	| Resize about the centre | Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag a handle. |
    92	| Cancel the drag | Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>. Everything goes back, with no undo step. |
    93	
    94	Each drag is one undo step, called Move Region or Resize Region. A side stays between 1 and 20,000 of the clip's own pixels.
    95	
    96	The outlines show only with exactly one clip selected, on an unlocked track, outside [crop mode](/canvas/crop/) and the text editor.
    97	
    98	The clip's own handles win where they overlap a region's. A drag inside a region, away from its grips, moves the clip. While Place on Canvas or Zoom to Region is on, it takes every press, and the outlines stay drawn underneath.
    99	
   100	## Remove a region
   101	
   102	Choose **Remove** in the region's row. It's one undo step, called Remove Region, and the regions after it renumber.
   103	
   104	**Reset** in the section's header clears every region on the clip.
   105	
   106	## Animate a region
   107	
   108	Each region's numbers can change over an [action](/motion/actions/), which is how a region follows something moving across the shot or fades in over a few seconds.
   109	
   110	With an action selected, the rows and the canvas grips set the action's end state:
   111	
   112	- **Amount**, **Feather**, **Center** and **Size** ramp to the new value along the action's curve.
   113	- **Shape** and the kind switch at the action's end. The other regions on the clip keep ramping.
   114	
   115	The inspector shows the value at the playhead, so a changed kind or shape reads as the old one until the playhead reaches the action's end.
   116	
   117	**Add Region**, **Place on Canvas** and **Remove** always change the clip itself, even with an action selected, because a list of regions can't ramp to a list of a different length. If an action already animates the regions, it keeps the count it had. The whole list then switches at the action's end instead of ramping. No grips show while the two counts differ, though the outlines stay.
   118	
   119	See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
   120	
   121	## Good to know
   122	
   123	- **Regions ride with the clip.** They stay on the same part of the picture through a move, a scale, a rotation and a [zoom](/motion/zoom-to-region/). A region drawn on a rotated clip is the box around your drag in the clip's own axes, so it turns with the clip and comes out larger than the rectangle you dragged.
   124	- **Cropping can shift a region.** A region is measured from the centre of the cropped picture, so cropping more off one side than the other moves the region across the picture by half the difference. Check your regions after a [crop](/canvas/crop/).
   125	- **Overlapping regions.** Where two overlap, whichever hides more wins, and two overlapping blurs add up. So the order of the regions doesn't matter, and there's no way to reorder them.
   126	- **Filters and the grade.** A region's colour is graded and filtered like the picture around it. A [Sharpen filter](/effects/filters/) can't bring the hidden detail back. On a clip with a Blur filter, a pixelated region's blocks aren't blurred.
   127	- **Pixelate's blocks sit on a grid across the whole picture.** Moving a region doesn't shift them, and its edge can cut through a block.
   128	- **Several clips selected.** Any change gives them all the same regions, taken from the first selected clip and replacing what the others had.
   129	- **What it works on.** Every clip that draws has the section, text and shapes included. It shows on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip but has no effect there, so set it on the clips inside. An adjustment clip has no **Picture** sub-tab.
   130	- **Missing files.** While a clip's file is missing, its slate shows without the regions.
   131	- **Copying regions.** [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) carries a clip's regions, along with the rest of its picture settings.
   132	
   133	## Related
   134	
   135	- [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/)
   136	- [Filters](/effects/filters/)
   137	- [Actions](/motion/actions/)
   138	- [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/)
     1	---
     2	title: Hide While Silent
     3	description: Fade a clip out in the pauses of someone's speech and back in just before they talk again.
     4	---
     5	
     6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
     7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
     8	
     9	Hide While Silent fades a clip out in the pauses of someone's speech and back in just before they talk again. Use it on a camera over a screen recording, so the presenter is there while they're talking and out of the way when they aren't.
    10	
    11	<AtAGlance
    12	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Hide While Silent"
    13	  tools={['set_video', 'set_media_speech']}
    14	  needs="Nothing. Frame Job finds the speech on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
    15	/>
    16	
    17	## Turn it on
    18	
    19	<Steps>
    20	
    21	1. Select the clip that should come and go, such as the camera.
    22	
    23	2. In the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, open the **Hide While Silent** section. It's shut until you open it.
    24	
    25	3. Tick **Hide while silent**.
    26	
    27	</Steps>
    28	
    29	The clip now follows the first file in [**Speech from**](#choose-which-file-to-follow), with the default [timing](#adjust-the-timing). The fade shows in the preview and in every export.
    30	
    31	The section's header reads **off**, **on** or the name of the file the clip follows. With several clips selected, ticking the box turns it on for each clip that's off, all following the same file.
    32	
    33	To turn it off, untick the box or choose **Reset** in the section's header.
    34	
    35	The checkbox is greyed in two cases, and its tooltip says which:
    36	
    37	| Tooltip | What it means |
    38	| --- | --- |
    39	| "No clip with sound plays under the selection." | Nothing with sound plays at the same time as the clip, so there's no speech to follow. |
    40	| "… speech has not been detected yet, so a clip cannot hide while it is silent. Try again in a moment." | Frame Job is still working through the file, which often happens straight after an import. |
    41	
    42	## Choose which file to follow
    43	
    44	**Speech from** lists the files with sound that play at the same time as the clip, on any track, one row each. The clip's own file is there too if it has sound. It's dimmed until **Hide while silent** is on.
    45	
    46	Files with no picture, such as a microphone recording, come first, then the file that plays alongside the clip for longest. A file you've already chosen stays in the list even if it no longer plays with the clip.
    47	
    48	If you pick a file whose speech Frame Job hasn't found yet, nothing changes and a note in the section says why.
    49	
    50	## Adjust the timing
    51	
    52	| Control | What it does | Default | Range | Quick picks |
    53	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    54	| **Pre-roll** | How long before each run of words the clip is fully back. | 0.2 s | 0 to 5 s | 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5 |
    55	| **Hold** | How long the clip stays after each run of words. | 1.5 s | 0 to 5 s | 0.5, 1, 1.5, 3 |
    56	| **Fade** | How long the clip takes to fade out and in. At 0 it's a straight cut. | 0.3 s | 0 to 5 s | 0, 0.15, 0.3, 0.5 |
    57	
    58	The fades sit outside the other two. The clip starts to fade out when **Hold** ends, and it finishes fading in **Pre-roll** before the first word.
    59	
    60	So short pauses never hide the clip. A pause no longer than **Pre-roll** plus **Hold** leaves it on screen, which is 1.7 s at the defaults. The clip only fades all the way out in a pause of at least **Pre-roll** plus **Hold** plus two **Fades**, which is 2.3 s. Anything in between is a partial dip.
    61	
    62	Each change is one undo step, called Hide While Silent. These rows belong to the clip, even with an [action](/motion/actions/) selected.
    63	
    64	## See it on the timeline
    65	
    66	A teal line runs across the picture part of the clip. Where it's at the top, the clip shows. Where it's at the bottom, the clip is hidden. The clip has to be [tall enough](/timeline/track-height/) to show the line.
    67	
    68	Inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/), a clip that follows a file outside the nest doesn't draw its line, though it still fades. See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/).
    69	
    70	## When the followed file stops playing
    71	
    72	Where the file doesn't play at all, the clip shows. There's no fade at that edge, so a hidden clip comes straight back when the file's clip ends. The clip also shows wherever the file has no saved speech.
    73	
    74	With [nests](/editing/nests/), Frame Job reads the file in the nearest place that plays it at that moment: the clip's own timeline, then each enclosing nest outward. So when a camera is inside a nest and the microphone isn't, the microphone outside is followed.
    75	
    76	## The fade stays out of Opacity
    77	
    78	The fade only touches the picture Frame Job draws. The clip's own **Opacity** in the [Transform section](/canvas/transform/) keeps its value. A clip at 50 % Opacity peaks at 50 % and fades from there.
    79	
    80	An [action](/motion/actions/) can't animate Hide While Silent, though it can still animate the clip's Opacity.
    81	
    82	## Good to know
    83	
    84	- **Where the speech comes from.** It's the same as [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/): the runs of words Frame Job finds in the file on this Mac when it's added. The first time a file is followed, those runs are saved in the project in the same undo step.
    85	- **Only what plays counts.** Speech in a part of the file you've trimmed or cut away doesn't bring the clip back. A muted clip of the file still counts, because the speech is read from the file, not the mix.
    86	- **Nest clips.** A nest clip has no picture of its own, so the section isn't offered for it, or for a selection that includes one. Set it on the clips inside.
    87	- **Removing the file.** [Removing the followed file](/projects/remove-media/) from the project turns Hide While Silent off on every clip that followed it.
    88	- **Copying.** A pasted clip keeps Hide While Silent only when the file it follows comes along too, and Frame Job brings that file with it. [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) works the same way.
    89	
    90	## With an agent
    91	
    92	`set_video` can point a clip at any file in the project that has sound, not only one playing alongside it. `set_media_speech` saves runs of speech you supply for a file, in place of the ones Frame Job found. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/) and [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).
    93	
    94	## Related
    95	
    96	- [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/)
    97	- [The Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/)
    98	- [Position, scale, rotation and opacity](/canvas/transform/)

     3	/// The canvas REGION mode (spec §4.2): drag a rectangle over the picture and
     4	/// something is done with it. Two things, so far — `Z` adds a zoom action
     5	/// that brings the rectangle to the canvas (`add_zoom_action`, road map 2's
     6	/// phase 3b), and the Obscure section's "Place on Canvas" appends the
     7	/// rectangle to `video.obscure` (phase 3c).
     8	///
     9	/// **Why one mode and not two.** Both are the same rectangle in the same
    10	/// frame — spec §5.3's Q, source pixels from the centre of the layer's
    11	/// cropped rect — dragged with the same gesture over the same picture. A
    12	/// second overlay with a second copy of the conversion is exactly the drift
    13	/// `CanvasSessions.swift` exists to prevent, so `ZoomRegionSession` carries a
    14	/// `CanvasRegionPurpose` and this file branches on it in one place: the
    15	/// commit at the bottom.
    16	///
    17	/// **Why it is not a `PreviewCanvasView` gesture**, and why every piece below
    18	/// has the shape it has: `EditorViewController+Eyedropper.swift` argues it in
    19	/// full and this file follows it deliberately rather than inventing a second
    20	/// shape for a modal canvas mode. The overlay's PRESENCE is the mode (an
    21	/// extension can hold no state, and a mode outlives a drag, so it is not a
    22	/// canvas session); it is installed through `armCanvasMode`, the one place
    23	/// that keeps two modal overlays from stacking; it takes first responder so
    24	/// Esc reaches it; it clears its callbacks before it is torn down from inside
    25	/// its own event handler; it hands focus back to the canvas overlay on the way
    26	/// out; and a `sync…` hook closes it when the selection it was armed for
    27	/// moves.
    28	///
    29	/// **The one thing it does differently.** The eyedropper takes a click and
    30	/// this takes a DRAG, so the session lives on the view between mouse-down and
    31	/// mouse-up, and the view is given five one-line closures instead of two: two
    32	/// coordinate conversions (only `PreviewCanvasView` may map points to canvas
    33	/// pixels, spec §11), the resolved frame it draws while dragging, and the two
    34	/// outcomes. None of them holds logic; each forwards to a named method here.
    35	extension EditorViewController {
    36	    /// The armed region mode. Nil is the answer to "is the mode on".
    37	    var canvasRegion: CanvasRegionView? {
    38	        canvasContainer.subviews.compactMap { $0 as? CanvasRegionView }.first
    39	    }
    40	
    41	    // MARK: - Commands
    42	
    43	    /// `Z`, and the action lane's Zoom to Region button.
    44	    ///
    45	    /// It TOGGLES, which the eyedropper had to learn the hard way: once focus
    46	    /// has left the overlay — a click in the inspector, a menu — Esc no
    47	    /// longer reaches it and the key that armed the mode is the only way back
    48	    /// out. Pressing it again while the OTHER purpose is armed switches
    49	    /// purpose rather than leaving two half-armed modes to reason about.
    50	    @objc func zoomToRegion(_ sender: Any?) { toggleRegionMode(.zoom) }
    51	
    52	    /// The Obscure section's "Place on Canvas": the same band, appended to
    53	    /// `video.obscure` instead of turned into an action.
    54	    @objc func placeObscureRegion(_ sender: Any?) { toggleRegionMode(.obscure) }
    55	
    56	    /// The Actions section's "Zoom Back": the null-region form of the same
    57	    /// op, at the playhead. No rectangle to drag, so no mode.
    58	    @objc func zoomBack(_ sender: Any?) { zoomBackCommand() }
    59	
    60	    private func toggleRegionMode(_ purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose) {
    61	        if let armed = canvasRegion {
    62	            let again = armed.purpose == purpose
    63	            endRegionMode()
    64	            if again { return }
    65	        }
    66	        beginRegionMode(purpose)
    67	    }
    68	
    69	    /// Arms the mode over the canvas pane.
    70	    ///
    71	    /// It refuses rather than putting up a crosshair that could only ever
    72	    /// beep — `beginChromaEyedropper`'s rule, and `addActionAtPlayheadCommand`
    73	    /// already refuses an action when the playhead is off the clip. There has
    74	    /// to be exactly one clip selected (a region belongs to one layer's
    75	    /// source pixels; two clips would be two different rectangles), it has to
    76	    /// be drawing at the playhead (`regionTarget` asks the canvas, so a
    77	    /// clip hidden behind an in/out range or on a locked track says no), and
    78	    /// an obscure region needs a free slot.
    79	    private func beginRegionMode(_ purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose) {
    80	        guard let target = regionTarget(), previewCanvas != nil else {
    81	            NSSound.beep()
    82	            return
    83	        }

    85	            NSSound.beep()
    86	            return
    87	        }
    88	        let region = CanvasRegionView(
    89	            purpose: purpose, clip: target.id, note: regionNote(purpose, clip: target.id))
    90	        // One-line forwards only (app/CLAUDE.md).

    97	        // armed eyedropper on the way, so the two modes cannot stack.

   102	    /// from a completed drag, and from `syncRegionMode`.

   123	    /// The band's second pill for one clip, or nil: a During motion moves the
   124	    /// clip under a zoom solved without it (spec §11, R5-4), and only a zoom
   125	    /// is solved.
   126	    private func regionNote(_ purpose: CanvasRegionPurpose, clip: UInt32) -> String? {
   127	        guard purpose == .zoom else { return nil }
   128	        let during = document?.editedProject.snapshot.clip(clip)?.videoProps.motion?.during
   129	        return during != nil ? CanvasRegionView.duringNote : nil
   130	    }
   131	
   132	    /// `add_zoom_action` with no region, at the playhead: the clip goes back
   133	    /// to its own base `scale`, `x` and `y` over the action's span. The core
   134	    /// reads an absent and an explicit null region the same way; the op
   135	    /// builder sends the null so a saved call says which it meant.
   136	    private func zoomBackCommand() {
   137	        guard let document = document, let box = regionTarget(),
   138	              let clip = document.editedProject.snapshot.clip(box.id)
   139	        else {
   140	            NSSound.beep()
   141	            return
   142	        }
   143	        let at = clip.clipTime(document.playhead)
   144	        document.applyEdit("Zoom Back", .addZoomAction(clip: clip.id, at: at, region: nil))
   145	        selectAddedAction(on: clip.id, at: at, countBefore: clip.actions.count)
   146	    }
   147	
   148	    // MARK: - What the mode is aimed at
   149	
   150	    /// The one layer a region may be drawn on: the single selected clip, on
   151	    /// screen at the playhead and not on a locked track.
   152	    ///
   153	    /// It is answered as a `CanvasLayerBox` rather than a `ClipSnapshot`
   154	    /// because the box IS the question — it exists only for a clip the recipe
   155	    /// put on the canvas at this instant, and it carries the EVALUATED
   156	    /// transform the rectangle has to be measured through
   157	    /// (`CanvasLayerBox.sourcePoint` says why that is the opposite of every
   158	    /// other canvas session).
   159	    private func regionTarget() -> CanvasLayerBox? {
   160	        guard let document = document, document.selection.count == 1,
   161	              let id = document.selection.first,
   162	              let clip = document.editedProject.snapshot.clip(id), clip.contains(document.playhead),
   163	              let box = previewCanvas?.box(for: id), !box.locked
   164	        else { return nil }
   165	        return box
   166	    }
   167	
   168	    /// The obscure list the mode would append to — the first selected clip
   169	    /// with pixels, read through the binding so a playhead inside an action
   170	    /// reads that action's end state and not the base props.
   171	    private func obscureRegions() -> [ObscureProps] {
   172	        inspector?.binding.videoProps.obscure ?? []
   173	    }
   174	
   175	    // MARK: - The overlay's five questions
   176	
   177	    /// The inverse, landed in the OVERLAY's own coordinates — which are the
   178	    /// canvas view's today (the overlay fills the canvas, both are flipped),
   179	    /// but the conversion is spelled out rather than assumed.
   180	    private func regionViewPoint(_ point: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
   181	        guard let canvas = previewCanvas, let region = canvasRegion else { return point }
   182	        return region.convert(canvas.canvasToView(point), from: canvas)
   183	    }
   184	
   185	    /// The rectangle the canvas will actually be showing once this zoom lands,
   186	    /// in canvas pixels — what the overlay strokes beside the band so a
   187	    /// freely dragged rectangle does not have to be guessed at.
   188	    private func regionResolvedFrame(_ session: ZoomRegionSession) -> CGRect? {
   189	        guard let box = previewCanvas?.box(for: session.clip),
   190	              let source = session.sourceRect(in: box)
   191	        else { return nil }
   192	        return session.frameRect(in: box, source: source)
   193	    }
   194	
   195	    // MARK: - The commit
   196	
   197	    /// One finished drag. `mouseUp` is an AppKit event, so both branches
   198	    /// commit through the ordinary (non-grouped) door and each is ONE undo
   199	    /// step; the eyedropper needs `applyGrouped` only because its answer comes
   200	    /// back off a queue.
   201	    ///
   202	    /// A band too small to mean anything leaves the mode ARMED and beeps —
   203	    /// a stray click is a miss, not a decision, which is the rule the
   204	    /// eyedropper states for a click that landed off the picture.
   205	    private func regionCommitted(_ session: ZoomRegionSession) {
   206	        guard let box = previewCanvas?.box(for: session.clip),
   207	              let region = session.region(in: box)
   208	        else {
   209	            NSSound.beep()
   210	            return
   211	        }
   212	        switch session.purpose {
   213	        case .zoom:
   214	            commitZoom(session, region: region)
   215	        case .obscure:
   216	            commitObscure(session, region: region)
   217	        }

   276	/// `CanvasOverlayView` keeps with `PreviewCanvasView`, and the reason the

   280	    /// branches on the session's copy.

   396	        guard band.width >= 1, band.height >= 1 else { return }

   406	            to: convert(CGPoint(x: canvasFrame.maxX, y: canvasFrame.maxY)))

   411	        // reads as a rendering artefact rather than as a second rectangle.
   412	        let dash: [CGFloat] = [4, 3]

The property stays on through the action, then goes off as it ends. The row shows ◆ and "at end".

This is different from [taking the row out of the action](#take-a-property-out-of-the-action), which stops the action changing the property at all.

## Read the row marks

Each row in the Clip tab has a narrow gutter to the left of its label. The mark there says how the row relates to the selected action.

| Mark | What it means | How else you can tell |
| --- | --- | --- |
### Clear and Reset

**Clear** and **Reset** share one place in a section's header, and at most one of them shows.

- While an action is selected, a section with rows that can animate shows **Clear** if the action animates anything in it, and neither button if it doesn't.
- A section of ⊘ rows keeps **Reset**, because its edits go to the clip.
- With no action selected, **Reset** shows only while the section differs from its defaults.

## Right-click a row

Right-click a row's label, slider, checkbox or the space beside them. Each item shows only where it applies, and a row with nothing to offer has no menu. A text field or a pop-up keeps its own right-click menu.

| Item | When it shows | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |

content.content:
### Hide while silent

A camera clip can fade out while nobody is talking and fade back in just before
speech starts. Select the camera and open the Clip tab's Picture sub-tab: the
**Hide While Silent** section comes after Layout, shut until you open it. It is
offered for any clip with a picture but a nest clip (set it on the clips inside
the nest).

- **Hide while silent** turns it on. The camera follows the first file in
  **Speech from** — the files with sound playing under the clip, the
  microphone (a file with no picture) first, then the one that plays under it
  longest. Off, or Reset, takes it away.
- **Speech from** picks another file to follow.
- **Pre-roll** (0.2 s to start) is how long before each run of words the
  camera is fully back; **Hold** (1.5 s) how long it stays after; **Fade**
  (0.3 s) how long it takes to fade out and in. Each is 0–5 s.

The speech is the same as Duck by Speech's: the runs of words Frame Job finds
in the file on this Mac when it is added (no key, nothing uploaded). The first
time a file is followed, those runs are saved in the project, in the same
**Undo** step. If the file's speech has not been found yet, the checkbox is
greyed, and its tooltip says to try again in a moment.

Where the file does not play at all, the camera shows. When the camera is
inside a nest and the microphone is not, the microphone outside is followed.
The timeline draws a teal line over the camera clip's picture: at the top the
camera shows, at the bottom it is hidden. The fade is only in the picture: the
Transform section's Opacity and the agent's `get_project` still show the
clip's own value, and an action cannot animate it.

*Agents:* `set_video {clips, patch: {hide_silent: {media, pre_roll?, hold?,
fade?}}}`, the times in ticks; `{hide_silent: null}` removes it. When the media
has no saved speech the tool saves it first in the same step, and it refuses a
media with no sound or one whose speech has not been found yet.

### Shadow

A drop shadow cast by the layer's own shape: the picture, the letters of a
text clip, or a shape's outline and fill.

### Obscure

Obscure hides a face, a password field or a phone number behind up to **four**
blurred or pixelated regions per clip.

- **Add Region** adds a 480 × 270 pixelated box at the centre of the layer.
- **Place on Canvas** arms a drawing mode ("Drag a rectangle to obscure · Esc
  to cancel"). Drag a rectangle over the selected clip to add a region there.
  A drag smaller than 6 px is treated as a miss, and the mode stays armed. The
  mode needs exactly one selected clip that is drawing at the playhead and has
  a free slot. Esc, a second press of the button, or a change of selection
  ends the mode, and so does the playhead leaving the clip.
- Only one canvas mode can be armed at a time: Place on Canvas, Zoom to
  Region (**Z**, see [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md)),
  Chroma Key's Pick from Canvas, and the qualifier's Pick from Canvas (see
  [Color grading](color-grading.md)). Arming one ends whichever other was
  armed.
- Each **Region N** row has a kind popup, **Pixelate** (hides) or **Blur**
  (softens), and a **Remove** button. Under it are **Shape** (Rectangle,
  Ellipse), **Amount** (0–100 %, default 100 %), **Feather** (0–200 px,
  default 20 px), **Center** (x, y) and **Size** (width, height, at least
  1 px).

On the canvas, the selected clip's regions are drawn as dashed outlines.
Drag a region's centre cross to move it. Drag one of its eight handles to
resize it, holding ⌥ to resize about its centre. The clip's own handles win
where they overlap a region, and a drag inside a region moves the clip. Esc
cancels the drag.

Regions are stored in the clip's own source pixels, so they follow the layer
through every move, scale, rotation and crop. Each region's numbers can be
animated like any other property. **Add Region**, **Place on Canvas** and
**Remove** always change the clip itself, not the selected action.

## Text clips

Press **T**, or use the timeline bar's **Add Text** button, to add a text clip
at the playhead. It goes on the front-most track if there is room, or on a new
track in front of everything if there isn't. The new clip:

- reads "Title" in Source Sans 3 Bold at 72 px, white, centred
- lasts 5 seconds
- is selected, so the **Text** sub-tab opens on it

A text clip has no source file, so you can trim it to any length.
Double-click it on the canvas to type (see
[Inline text editing](#inline-text-editing)).

*Agents:* `add_text_clip` (track, at, optional duration and text, either a
plain string or a text patch); `set_text` to restyle.

### The Text tab

| Section | Rows |
|---|---|
| **Content** | A multi-line text area. Return, Tab or a click away applies it and gives the keys back to the editor; ⇧Return, ⌘Return, ⌥Return or ⌃Return starts a new line |
| **Font** | **Family** (every font installed on the Mac, plus the faces the app ships with: Source Sans 3, Source Serif 4, Montserrat, Anton, Bebas Neue, Darker Grotesque and IBM Plex Mono), **Style** (that family's faces), **Size** 6–800 px |
| **Style** | **Color**, **Align** (L / C / R), **Vertical** (top / middle / bottom within the box), **UPPERCASE**, **Line spacing** 0.5–4× (default 1), **Tracking** −20 to 100 px (default 0) |
| **Outline** | **Outline** on/off, **Width** 0–40 px (default 2), **Color** (default black) |
| **Backdrop** | A plate behind the text: **Backdrop** on/off, **Fill** (default black at 60 %), **Padding** 0–200 px (default 12), **Radius** 0–200 px (default 8) |
| **Box** | **Mode**: **Auto-size** (the box fits the words) or **Fixed width** (the words wrap). **Width** is 20–20000 px, starting at 60 % of the canvas width |
| **Reveal** | How the text arrives and leaves: **None**, **Typewriter**, **Word Fade** or **Line Rise**, with separate **In** and **Out** durations (0–10 s; In defaults to 1 s and Out to 0) measured from the clip's first and last frame |
| **Presets** | One-click looks, described below |

UPPERCASE changes only how the text is drawn: what you typed is kept as typed.
A text clip also gets the Picture tab's Transform, Shadow, Filters,
Reflection, Spotlight and Obscure sections.
